data.content_ref: inline:The isolated artifact shares mechanism with SRC_003's injected-false-claim methodology but relocates it from a population-level statistical test to a single-run causal-graph test: instead of injecting many false claims to measure rejection rate, inject a single false claim and trace whether the verdict's causal dependency graph (constructed from the run record's intermediate states) reroutes through the injected signal. The shared mechanism is causal sensitivity to falsification, but the operationalization differs: SRC_003 requires statistical power across trials, while the isolated artifact requires causal-path coverage within one trial. This integrates SRC_003's skepticism with SRC_002's single-run diagnostics by showing that a single injected false claim can serve as a sufficient negative control if the run record is rich enough to trace the causal path from injection to verdict. This is REFUTED IF the causal-path trace cannot distinguish rerouting through the injected signal from rerouting through a confounding intermediate state — i.e., if the single-run causal graph is underdetermined and multiple injection paths are compatible with the same run record.
